items.title: Traditionally, how have Australian doctors differed from doctors in many Western countries?
options: They have worked closely with pharmaceutical companies.
They have often worked alongside other therapists.
They have been reluctant to accept alternative therapists.
They have regularly prescribed alternative remedies.

items.title: In 1990, Americans
options: were prescribed more herbal medicines than in previous years.
consulted alternative therapists more often than doctors.
spent more on natural therapies than orthodox medicines.
made more complaints about doctors than in previous years.

items: Australians have been turning to alternative therapies in increasing numbers over the past 20 years.
Between 1983 and 1990 the numbers of patients visiting alternative therapists rose to include a further 8% of the population.
The 1990 survey related to 550,000 consultations with alternative therapists.
In the past, Australians had a higher opinion of doctors than they do today.
Some Australian doctors are retraining in alternative therapies.
Alternative therapists earn higher salaries than doctors.
The 1993 Sydney survey involved 289 patients who visited alternative therapists for acupuncture treatment.
All the patients in the 1993 Sydney survey had long-term medical complaints.
